# integration-esphome

A [MajorDom](https://majordom.io) integration — bridges **ESPHome** devices into the
MajorDom language.

Built for the **MajorDom Hub**, but it doesn't need it: this is a standalone, standardized
library for ESPHome that you can use on its own (see **Run it standalone** below). Built on the
[MajorDom Integration SDK](https://github.com/MajorDom-Systems/integration-sdk). The entry point
is `ESPHomeController` (`majordom_esphome/controller.py`), which the Hub — or the SDK's dev
runner — instantiates and drives through its lifecycle: discovery → pairing → commands →
teardown.

- **Other protocols:** browse the [MajorDom integrations](https://github.com/orgs/MajorDom-Systems/repositories?q=integration-).
- **Create your own:** start from the [integration template](https://github.com/MajorDom-Systems/integration-template).

## Documentation

Full integration-author docs — the controller lifecycle, data models, storing data, discovery,
and a worked example — live at **[docs.majordom.io](https://docs.majordom.io/device-integration)**.

## Development

```sh
poetry install && poetry run poe install
```

| Task | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `poe check` | Full quality pipeline (ruff, ty, pytest, poetry build/check) |
| `poe check --ci` | Same, plus `git diff --exit-code` |

Work lands on `develop`; `master` is protected and released via **Actions → Release**.

Tests drive the controller with the SDK's test doubles against a **virtual ESPHome device**: a
native binary built from `tests/virtual/sketches/*.yaml` (ESPHome `host` platform, one entity of
every supported kind, with and without API encryption) — no physical hardware required. The
binaries are built on first use and need the ESPHome CLI:

```sh
pipx install esphome && poetry run python -m tests.virtual.build
```

Host nodes have no BLE, so the Improv tests run the real client against a scripted Improv GATT service. End-to-end
tests on real hardware are kept in a private repository.

## Run it standalone (without the Hub)

`majordom-esphome` is a standalone library — import it into your own app, or run **just this
integration** interactively (discover, pair, control, and inspect devices from a prompt) with no
Hub. It needs ESPHome devices reachable on the local network (Wi-Fi or Ethernet).

See **[Standalone mode](https://docs.majordom.io/device-integration/standalone)** for the
interactive CLI, watch mode, and the programmatic API.

## Supported transports

The integration speaks the **ESPHome native API** over TCP (port `6053` by default), with or without
Noise encryption. Devices must have the `api:` component enabled in their YAML; an API-less device
(e.g. web server only) is not supported.

## About this integration

- **Protocol / platform:** ESPHome native API (`aioesphomeapi`).
- **Transport(s):** TCP/IP (Wi-Fi, Ethernet); devices are found via mDNS (`_esphomelib._tcp`). Nodes without
Wi-Fi yet are found over BLE (Improv) and set up onto the Hub's Wi-Fi (see below).
- **Supported entities:** light (on/off, brightness, RGB), switch, sensor, binary sensor, text
sensor, number, select, button, cover (position), fan (on/off), climate (mode, targets).
Every other entity the library knows (lock, valve, text, alarm panel, update, ...) is mapped generically from
the library's own types (see below); cameras and events are skipped.
- **Credentials needed to pair:** the API encryption key (type `secret`) if the node has one
configured in its YAML; otherwise none.
- **Encryption keys:** a node with `api: encryption:` but no `key:` (it announces `api_encryption_supported`) is given a
key of the integration's own at pairing: generated, stored on the device record, then set with
`noise_encryption_set_key` over a Noise session with the well-known all-zeros PSK (in plaintext on firmware that does
not announce `api_provisioning=zero-psk`). From then on the node accepts only that key, so the user never types one;
the key is stored before it is set, so a failed attempt (or a Hub restart in between) does not lock the Hub out. A node
without `encryption:` still pairs in plaintext, with a warning in the log to turn encryption on.
- **Wi-Fi setup over BLE (Improv):** a node built with `esp32_improv` (`improv_ble` from ESPHome 2026.11) and no Wi-Fi
networks advertises the Improv service; it is offered as a `ble` discovery named (and identified) by its node name.
Pairing it gives it the Hub's Wi-Fi with [`py-improv-ble-client`](https://github.com/home-assistant-libs/py-improv-ble-client)
(asking the user to press its button when it has an `authorizer`), waits for it to announce itself over mDNS (matched
by the name it advertised, which ESPHome cuts to 20 characters), then pairs it like any other node, keyless key
included. The Hub's device takes the node's own identity (`pair_device` returns it). The Wi-Fi comes from the Hub's
`wifi_credentials` dependency (SDK `feature/wifi-credentials`); a Hub without one cannot set nodes up over BLE.

### Required harness

- **Hardware adapters:** none — ESPHome devices are self-contained and connect over the network.
- **Third-party software services:** none — the integration speaks directly to ESPHome devices.
- **OS / permissions:** network access to the ESPHome devices (same LAN or routable subnet);
mDNS/SSDP may be required for discovery depending on configuration.

### Protocol stack (OSI)

Every integration is two things stacked: the **MajorDom integration layer** — mapping the
protocol to MajorDom's domain model — sitting on top of the **protocol stack** it bridges. The
top layer is *always this repo*.

| Layer | Protocol | Implemented by |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| **MajorDom integration** | maps ESPHome ↔ MajorDom domain model | **this repo, always** |
| Application (7) | ESPHome Native API | [`aioesphomeapi`](https://github.com/esphome/aioesphomeapi) |
| Transport (4) | TCP | OS / device firmware |
| Network (3) | IP (IPv4 / IPv6) | OS / device firmware |
| Data link / Physical (1–2) | Wi-Fi (802.11) or Ethernet | device hardware |

### Progress

Two checklists. An item is ticked only when a test in `tests/` proves it.

**Implementation** — makes the integration functional:

- [x] Discovery service registered via `self.dependencies.zeroconf_discovery_service`; the cancel
closure is called in `stop`
- [x] Discovery listener methods fire when nodes appear, change and leave, and the controller calls
the matching `self.dependencies.output.controller_did_*_discovery`
- [x] Paired devices reconnect when the Hub restarts (`controller_did_connect_device` is called)
- [x] `start_pairing_window`: not needed, mDNS and BLE discovery are always on (SDK default is a no-op)
- [x] Device pairing, including the encryption key (`CredentialsType.secret`), and a generated key for keyless nodes
- [x] Device schema is mapped from the entities the device reports: parameters, units, limits and
valid values
- [x] Hub → Device control (`send_command`)
- [x] Device → Hub event subscription (`controller_did_receive_events` on every state change)
- [x] `identify`: ESPHome has no identify action, so it is a documented no-op
- [x] `unpair`
- [x] `fetch` reports the current value of every parameter in one batch
- [x] Paired devices going offline / coming back online while the Hub is running update
`device.available` and `last_error`, and call `controller_did_lose_device` /
`controller_did_connect_device`
- [x] Graceful shutdown in `stop`: discovery stopped, connections closed, no tasks left running
- [x] Tests pass against a virtual ESPHome device (`tests/`)
- [x] README matches the code

**Quality** — makes it reliable and maintainable (the bar for release):

- [x] **Recovers automatically** from connection loss / offline device / restarted device: retried
with exponential backoff (1 s up to 30 s), no manual restart
- [x] **No exception escapes** discovery handlers, state callbacks or background tasks
- [x] **Failures are surfaced** on the device (`available` / `last_error`) in plain language and
cleared on recovery; a rejected encryption key is reported as such
- [x] **Fully asynchronous**: no blocking I/O on the event loop
- [x] **Stable identity**: device and parameter UUIDs derive through the SDK helpers
(`device_uuid`, `parameter_uuid`) from the node's MAC address and the entity's `object_id`
- [x] **End-to-end tests** drive discovery (over a stubbed zeroconf, never the real network) → pair → state → command →
fetch → restart → outage → `unpair` against a virtual device, with and without encryption
- [x] **Failure paths tested**: unreachable device, wrong or missing key, a key the node refuses, a node unreachable
after it took its key, unsupported credentials,
command on a read-only parameter, out-of-range values, offline device
- [x] **Broad device coverage**: the entities above by hand, every other entity generically (tested with a lock, valve, text, date and alarm panel)
- [x] **Readable & structured**: conversion logic in a mapper, models separated
- [x] **Efficient**: subscriptions instead of polling; states are delivered in order
- [x] **Diagnosable**: connection failures and unexpected errors are logged with their cause
- [x] **Parameter metadata**: `visibility` follows the entity category, and `main_parameter` is a
one-tap toggle
- [x] **Owned**: maintained by Parker Industries, who keep it working as ESPHome and the library evolve

### Parameter mapping

Parameters are built from what the device reports (`list_entities_services`), never from fixed
defaults:

| Entity | Parameters |
|--------|------------|
| switch, fan | `state` (bool) |
| light | `state`, `brightness` (%) if the light dims, `color_hue` (°) and `color_saturation` (%) if it supports RGB; settings: `transition_length` (s, kept by the integration and added to every later command of the light) and `flash` (a `struct` command with its `length` as argument) |
| cover | `position` (%), `operation` (`IDLE` / `IS_OPENING` / `IS_CLOSING`, read-only) |
| climate | `mode` (`enum` of the modes it supports), `current_temperature`, `target_temperature` or `target_temperature_low/high` |
| number | `state` with the device's `min` / `max` / `step` |
| select | `state` as the option index (`enum`, `valid_values` labels are the options) |
| sensor, binary sensor, text sensor | `state` (read-only) |
| button | `state` (fires the press) |

Brightness, positions and saturation are percentages (0–100, ESPHome reports 0–1); colour is hue in degrees
plus saturation, the model the Matter and Zigbee integrations use, converted from ESPHome's RGB. Enums are
integers with string labels in `valid_values`, labelled by the ESPHome enum names. A command may give an enum value as its key or its label (the option or member name). Units come from the
entity's own unit string, else from its device class. Entities in the
`config` / `diagnostic` category are `setting`, and entities disabled by default are `system`.

### Remaining fields

The hand-written mapping above gives the everyday parameters. Every other state or command field an entity supports is
added by the generic mapping as a `setting` parameter (`majordom_esphome/generic.py`), so nothing the library reports is
dropped silently: a fan's speed level, direction, oscillation and presets; a cover's tilt and stop; a light's colour
temperature, white and effects; a climate's action, fan, swing and preset modes and humidity. A water heater's state bit mask becomes `on` and `away` switches; a
date or time is one `struct` parameter whose fields are its parts; a command that needs a code (a lock or alarm panel
that requires one) is a `command_with_code` `struct` command with the command and the code as arguments, next to a
`code` setting holding a default code: a code typed with the command wins, else the default is sent with every command
of the entity, so one-tap actions and automations work once the user opts in. Commands with arguments are `struct`
parameters with the arguments as `fields`, as the SDK describes. A field is only added when
the entity says it supports it, enums are limited to the supported members, option lists (effects, presets) become
enums like a select, and the limits the entity reports (speed count, mireds, humidity) are used. The few fields that
are exposed under another name or not at all (RGB channels, deprecated fields) are listed with the reason in
`UNMAPPED` in the catalogue, which fails when a new field appears that is neither mapped nor explained.

### Generic mapping

Entities without a hand-written mapping get parameters from `aioesphomeapi`'s own types (`majordom_esphome/generic.py`):
one parameter per field of the entity's state (read-only, unless the entity's command accepts it) and one per
command argument that can be sent on its own. `bool`, `int`, `float` and `str` map directly, the library's integer
enums become `enum` parameters labelled with their member names, fractions such as a position or volume become
percentages, and a command-only flag (a valve's `stop`) becomes a button. Commands with several required arguments
(a date) are read-only. A hand-written mapping wins wherever the generic result is not good enough for the user.

### Entity catalogue

`tests/test_catalogue.py` and `tests/virtual/catalogue.py` mirror the Matter integration's virtual-device catalogue.
The list of entity kinds is whatever the installed `aioesphomeapi` knows. Fast checks (always run) fail when a kind is
neither mapped by the integration nor skipped on purpose, or has neither a recipe nor a reason it cannot run on the
host node. Recipes are written by hand, never guessed: each one switches on every capability of its entity and comes
with the exact parameters it must produce (`EXPECTED`) and every state or command field that is deliberately not
exposed, with the reason (`UNMAPPED`), so a field ESPHome adds later fails the sweep until it is mapped or explained. The sweep (`poetry run pytest -m catalogue`) builds one virtual node per recipe in parallel, pairs it, checks
its parameters against `EXPECTED` and `UNMAPPED`, reads its states, sends a valid command to every control parameter and checks that the connection survives and every value
has the declared type. `.github/workflows/canary.yml` runs everything monthly against the latest ESPHome and
`aioesphomeapi` and goes red when upstream adds something unsupported.

### Notes

The device id derives from the node's MAC address (mDNS `mac` TXT record) via the SDK's UUID
helpers, so ids are stable across restarts and namespaced per integration.

ESPHome devices must have the `api:` component enabled in their YAML.

Connecting: a node is reached through its hostname first, then through the IP addresses it announced.
The first address that works moves to the front and the ones that failed move to the end, so the
next connection starts with what worked last time. When a paired node announces itself again (e.g.
after a DHCP change) its address list is refreshed.

See [LICENSE](LICENSE). For commercial licensing or partnership inquiries regarding MajorDom,
contact us via [parker-industries.org/partnership](https://parker-industries.org/partnership).

# FILE: majordom_esphome/__init__.py
================================================================================
from majordom_integration_sdk import Peripheral, Platform

from .controller import ESPhomeController

__all__ = ["ESPhomeController", "peripherals"]


def peripherals(platform: Platform) -> list[Peripheral]:
    return [ESPhomeController(platform)]


================================================================================
# FILE: majordom_esphome/bluetooth.py
================================================================================
"""ESPHome nodes with ``bluetooth_proxy`` as Bluetooth sources: the hub hears and reaches BLE devices
through them as if through its own adapter.

A node serves one API connection at a time (the newest subscriber wins), so it can't serve this hub
and another one together.
"""

import contextlib
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable

from aioesphomeapi import (
    APIClient,
    APIConnectionError,
    BluetoothGATTService,
    BluetoothLERawAdvertisementsResponse,
    BluetoothProxyFeature,
)
from bleak.backends.device import BLEDevice
from bleak.backends.scanner import AdvertisementData
from bluetooth_data_tools import int_to_bluetooth_address, parse_advertisement_data_bytes
from majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities import GattCharacteristic, GattService, OnAdvertisement

_PROPERTIES = {0x02: "read", 0x04: "write-without-response", 0x08: "write", 0x10: "notify", 0x20: "indicate"}
_CCCD = "00002902-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb"
_CONNECTS = BluetoothProxyFeature.ACTIVE_CONNECTIONS | BluetoothProxyFeature.REMOTE_CACHING
_REMEMBERED = 1024  # devices kept merged; phones rotate their address, so the oldest are dropped


class ESPhomeBLEConnection:
    def __init__(self, client: APIClient, address: int, mtu: int, unsubscribe: Callable[[], None]):
        self._client, self._address, self.mtu, self._unsubscribe = client, address, mtu or 23, unsubscribe
        self._services: list[BluetoothGATTService] | None = None
        self._notifying: dict[int, Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]] = {}  # handle -> stop

    async def _gatt_services(self) -> list[BluetoothGATTService]:
        if self._services is None:  # the proxy forgets them once sent
            self._services = (await self._client.bluetooth_gatt_get_services(self._address)).services
        return self._services

    async def services(self) -> list[GattService]:
        return [
            GattService(s.uuid, s.handle, tuple(
                GattCharacteristic(c.uuid, c.handle, tuple(n for bit, n in _PROPERTIES.items() if c.properties & bit))
                for c in s.characteristics
            ))
            for s in await self._gatt_services()
        ]  # fmt: skip

    async def read(self, handle: int) -> bytes:
        return bytes(await self._client.bluetooth_gatt_read(self._address, handle))

    async def write(self, handle: int, data: bytes, is_response_needed: bool = True):
        await self._client.bluetooth_gatt_write(self._address, handle, data, is_response_needed)

    async def start_notify(self, handle: int, callback: Callable[[bytes], None]):
        characteristics = (c for s in await self._gatt_services() for c in s.characteristics)
        if (characteristic := next((c for c in characteristics if c.handle == handle), None)) is None:
            raise LookupError(f"The device has no characteristic {handle}")
        stop, _ = await self._client.bluetooth_gatt_start_notify(self._address, handle, lambda _, d: callback(bytes(d)))
        self._notifying[handle] = stop
        # the proxy leaves the client characteristic configuration to the client
        if cccd := next((d.handle for d in characteristic.descriptors if d.uuid == _CCCD), None):
            indicate = characteristic.properties & 0x20 and not characteristic.properties & 0x10
            await self._client.bluetooth_gatt_write_descriptor(
                self._address, cccd, b"\x02\x00" if indicate else b"\x01\x00"
            )

    async def stop_notify(self, handle: int):
        if stop := self._notifying.pop(handle, None):
            await stop()

    async def disconnect(self):
        # the library drops the notify handlers once told the device disconnected, which unsubscribing stops
        self._client.bluetooth_gatt_stop_notify_for_address(self._address)
        self._unsubscribe()
        await self._client.bluetooth_device_disconnect(self._address)


class ESPhomeBLESource:
    """An ESPHome node lends its Bluetooth radio to the hub: what it hears and the connections it makes become one
    more source of the hub's Bluetooth router, offered to it as ``ble/esphome-proxy``."""

    def __init__(self, client: APIClient, mac: str, features: BluetoothProxyFeature):
        self.mac = mac  # of its Bluetooth radio
        self.name = f"esphome:{mac}"
        self._client, self._features = client, features
        self._unsubscribe: Callable[[], None] | None = None
        self._unsubscribe_slots: Callable[[], None] | None = None
        self._paused = False
        self.free_slots: int | None = None  # connections it can still open, as the node last said
        # its loss shows through the node's API connection: the router never resubscribes it for hearing no one
        self.is_loss_reported = True
        self._heard: dict[str, tuple[AdvertisementData, int]] = {}  # address -> merged advertisement, address type

    async def start(self, on_advertisement: OnAdvertisement):
        def on_advertisements(response: BluetoothLERawAdvertisementsResponse):
            advertisements = response.advertisements
            for i in range(len(advertisements)):  # iterating the protobuf directly costs a debug log per batch
                raw = advertisements[i]
                address = int_to_bluetooth_address(raw.address)
                device, adv = self._merge(address, raw.address_type, raw.rssi, raw.data)
                if not self._paused:
                    on_advertisement(device, adv)

        self._unsubscribe = self._client.subscribe_bluetooth_le_raw_advertisements(on_advertisements)
        if self._features & _CONNECTS == _CONNECTS:
            self._unsubscribe_slots = self._client.subscribe_bluetooth_connections_free(self._on_slots)

    def _on_slots(self, free: int, limit: int, allocated: list[int]):
        self.free_slots = free

    def _merge(self, address: str, address_type: int, rssi: int, data: bytes) -> tuple[BLEDevice, AdvertisementData]:
        # packets and scan responses arrive apart; merged like BlueZ does, so they don't read as changes
        name, uuids, service_data, manufacturer_data, tx_power = parse_advertisement_data_bytes(data)
        if previous := self._heard.pop(address, None):  # re-added last: the dict stays oldest first
            before = previous[0]
            name = name or before.local_name
            uuids = sorted({*before.service_uuids, *uuids})
            service_data = before.service_data | service_data
            manufacturer_data = before.manufacturer_data | manufacturer_data
            tx_power = before.tx_power if tx_power is None else tx_power
        adv = AdvertisementData(name, dict(manufacturer_data), dict(service_data), list(uuids), tx_power, rssi, ())
        self._heard[address] = adv, address_type
        if len(self._heard) > _REMEMBERED:
            del self._heard[next(iter(self._heard))]
        return BLEDevice(address, name, {"source": self.name}), adv

    async def stop(self):
        for unsubscribe in (self._unsubscribe, self._unsubscribe_slots):
            if unsubscribe:
                with contextlib.suppress(APIConnectionError):
                    unsubscribe()
        self._unsubscribe = self._unsubscribe_slots = None

    async def pause_scanning(self):
        # muted, not unsubscribed: the node answers connects only to its subscriber, and stops scanning itself
        # while it connects
        self._paused = True

    async def resume_scanning(self):
        self._paused = False

    async def connect(self, address: str, on_disconnect: Callable[[], None]) -> ESPhomeBLEConnection:
        if self._features & _CONNECTS != _CONNECTS:
            raise ConnectionError(f"{self.name} only listens")
        handle = int(address.replace(":", ""), 16)
        states: list[tuple[bool, int, int]] = []

        def on_state(connected: bool, mtu: int, error: int):
            states.append((connected, mtu, error))
            if len(states) > 1 and not connected:
                on_disconnect()

        unsubscribe = await self._client.bluetooth_device_connect(
            handle, on_state, feature_flags=self._features, address_type=self._heard.get(address, (None, 0))[1]
        )  # returns once the proxy answered: connected or not
        connected, mtu, error = states[0]
        if not connected:
            unsubscribe()
            raise ConnectionError(f"{self.name} can't connect to {address} (error {error})")
        return ESPhomeBLEConnection(self._client, handle, mtu, unsubscribe)


async def ble_source_of(client: APIClient) -> ESPhomeBLESource | None:
    """The node's source, if it lends Bluetooth this hub can use."""
    info = await client.device_info()
    if (version := client.api_version) is None:  # the connection closed meanwhile
        return None
    features = BluetoothProxyFeature(info.bluetooth_proxy_feature_flags_compat(version))
    if not features & BluetoothProxyFeature.RAW_ADVERTISEMENTS:  # no proxy, or firmware too old to stream them
        return None
    return ESPhomeBLESource(client, info.bluetooth_mac_address or info.mac_address, features)

# FILE: majordom_esphome/connection.py
================================================================================
import asyncio
import contextlib
import logging
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID

from aioesphomeapi import (
    APIClient,
    APIConnectionError,
    EntityInfo,
    EntityState,
    InvalidEncryptionKeyAPIError,
    RequiresEncryptionAPIError,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class _HideKeySetting(logging.Filter):
    """The library logs every message it sends at DEBUG: never let the one carrying a new key through."""

    def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool:
        return "NoiseEncryptionSetKeyRequest" not in record.getMessage()


logging.getLogger("aioesphomeapi.connection").addFilter(_HideKeySetting())

ADDRESS_TIMEOUT = 3.0  # seconds, per address: a dead address must not delay the next one
WAIT_READY_TIMEOUT = 30.0
RECONNECT_DELAY_FIRST = 1.0
RECONNECT_DELAY_MAX = 30.0

StateCallback = Callable[[UUID, EntityInfo, EntityState], Awaitable[None]]
AvailabilityCallback = Callable[[UUID, bool, str | None], Awaitable[None]]  # (device id, available, reason if not)
AddressesCallback = Callable[[UUID, list[str]], Awaitable[None]]
ClientCallback = Callable[[UUID, APIClient | None], Awaitable[None]]  # (device id, its client if connected, else None)


class KeyRefusedError(ConnectionError):
    """A keyless node did not take the encryption key it was given."""


def describe_error(exc: BaseException) -> str:
    """Plain-language reason for the user; the technical detail stays in the logs."""
    if isinstance(exc, KeyRefusedError):
        return "The device refused the new encryption key"
    if isinstance(exc, RequiresEncryptionAPIError):
        return "The device requires an encryption key"
    if isinstance(exc, InvalidEncryptionKeyAPIError):
        return "The device rejected the encryption key"
    if isinstance(exc, TimeoutError):
        return "The device did not respond in time"
    return "The device is not reachable"


class ESPhomeDeviceConnection:
    """One device's native-API session: connects, keeps reconnecting with backoff, and feeds states to a callback."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        device_id: UUID,
        addresses: list[str],
        port: int,
        encryption_key: str | None,
        on_state: StateCallback,
        on_availability: AvailabilityCallback | None = None,
        on_addresses: AddressesCallback | None = None,
        on_client: ClientCallback | None = None,
    ):
        self.device_id = device_id
        self.addresses = list(addresses)  # hostname and IPs, tried in order; reordered by what worked
        self.port = port
        self.encryption_key = encryption_key
        self.on_state_callback = on_state
        self.on_availability_callback = on_availability
        self.on_addresses_callback = on_addresses
        self.on_client_callback = on_client

        self.last_error: Exception | None = None
        self._client: APIClient | None = None
        self._task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
        self._consumer: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
        self._entities: dict[int, EntityInfo] = {}
        self._states: asyncio.Queue[EntityState] = asyncio.Queue()
        self._ready = asyncio.Event()
        self._failed = asyncio.Event()
        self._disconnected = asyncio.Event()
        self._available: bool | None = None  # what the callback was last told
        self._reported_client: APIClient | None = None  # what the client callback was last told

    @property
    def ready(self) -> bool:
        return self._ready.is_set()

    async def start(self):
        self._failed.clear()
        self.last_error = None
        self._consumer = asyncio.create_task(self._consume_states())
        self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run())

    async def stop(self):
        for task in (self._task, self._consumer):
            if task is not None:
                task.cancel()
                with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                    await task
        self._task = self._consumer = None
        await self._close_client()
        self._ready.clear()

    async def wait_ready(self, timeout: float = WAIT_READY_TIMEOUT):
        """Wait for the first successful connection; fail as soon as an attempt fails (no endless retrying)."""
        waiters = {asyncio.create_task(self._ready.wait()), asyncio.create_task(self._failed.wait())}
        try:
            await asyncio.wait(waiters, timeout=timeout, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
        finally:
            for waiter in waiters:
                waiter.cancel()
        if self._ready.is_set():
            return
        if self.last_error is not None:
            raise ConnectionError(describe_error(self.last_error)) from self.last_error
        raise TimeoutError("The device did not respond in time")

    async def provision_key(self, key: str, session_psk: str | None):
        """Give a keyless node its key over a short-lived session (`session_psk`: the zero PSK, or None for plaintext on
        older firmware). The node stores it and accepts only connections with it from then on."""
        error: Exception = ConnectionError("The device has no address")
        for address in self.addresses:
            try:
                accepted = await self._set_key_at(address, key, session_psk)
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.info(f"Device {self.device_id} is not reachable at {address}: {exc!r}")
                error = exc
                continue
            if not accepted:
                raise KeyRefusedError(f"Device {self.device_id} refused the encryption key")
            self.encryption_key = key
            return
        raise error

    async def _set_key_at(self, address: str, key: str, session_psk: str | None) -> bool:
        dropped = asyncio.Event()

        async def on_stop(expected_disconnect: bool):
            dropped.set()

        client = APIClient(address, self.port, None, noise_psk=session_psk)
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(ADDRESS_TIMEOUT):
                await client.connect(login=True, on_stop=on_stop)
                accepted = await client.noise_encryption_set_key(key.encode())
            if accepted:  # the node switches to the key a moment later, then drops every session: connecting
                with contextlib.suppress(TimeoutError):  # before that would still meet the old (zero) PSK
                    async with asyncio.timeout(ADDRESS_TIMEOUT):
                        await dropped.wait()
            return accepted
        finally:
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                await client.disconnect()

    def get_entities(self) -> dict[int, EntityInfo]:
        return self._entities.copy()

    async def send_command(self, entity_key: int, component_type: str, command_args: dict[str, Any]):
        if self._client is None or not self.ready:
            raise ConnectionError("Device not connected")
        method = getattr(self._client, f"{component_type}_command", None)
        if method is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown component type: {component_type}")
        try:
            method(**command_args)  # fire-and-forget: the device answers with a state update
        except APIConnectionError as exc:
            raise ConnectionError("Device not connected") from exc

    async def _run(self):
        delay = RECONNECT_DELAY_FIRST
        while True:
            try:
                await self._connect()
                delay = RECONNECT_DELAY_FIRST
                await self._disconnected.wait()
                raise ConnectionError("connection lost")
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                raise
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.warning(f"Connection to {self.device_id} ({self.addresses}, port {self.port}) failed: {exc!r}")
                self.last_error = exc
                self._ready.clear()
                self._failed.set()
                await self._close_client()
                await self._report_availability(False, describe_error(exc))
                await asyncio.sleep(delay)
                delay = min(delay * 2, RECONNECT_DELAY_MAX)

    async def _connect(self):
        """Connect through the first address that works; remember what worked for the next connection."""
        self._disconnected.clear()
        failed: list[str] = []
        error: Exception = ConnectionError("The device has no address")
        for address in list(self.addresses):
            try:
                async with asyncio.timeout(ADDRESS_TIMEOUT):
                    await self._connect_to(address)
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.info(f"Device {self.device_id} is not reachable at {address}: {exc!r}")
                error = exc
                failed.append(address)
                await self._close_client()
                continue
            await self._remember(address, failed)
            await self._report_client(self._client)
            return
        raise error

    async def _connect_to(self, address: str):
        client = APIClient(address, self.port, None, noise_psk=self.encryption_key)
        self._client = client
        await client.connect(login=True, on_stop=self._on_stop)
        entities, _services = await client.list_entities_services()
        self._entities = {entity.key: entity for entity in entities}
        client.subscribe_states(self._state_received)
        self.last_error = None
        self._ready.set()
        logger.info(f"Connected to ESPHome device {self.device_id} at {address}:{self.port}")

    async def _remember(self, address: str, failed: list[str]):
        """Working address first, addresses that failed this time last."""
        untried = [a for a in self.addresses if a != address and a not in failed]
        remembered = [address, *untried, *failed]
        if remembered != self.addresses:
            self.addresses = remembered
            if self.on_addresses_callback is not None:
                try:
                    await self.on_addresses_callback(self.device_id, remembered)
                except Exception:
                    logger.exception(f"Error saving the addresses of {self.device_id}")
        await self._report_availability(True, None)

    async def _on_stop(self, expected_disconnect: bool):
        logger.info(f"Device {self.device_id} disconnected (expected={expected_disconnect})")
        self._ready.clear()
        self._disconnected.set()

    def _state_received(self, state: EntityState):
        self._states.put_nowait(state)

    async def _consume_states(self):
        """Deliver states one at a time, in the order the device sent them."""
        while True:
            state = await self._states.get()
            entity = self._entities.get(state.key)
            if entity is None:
                continue
            try:
                await self.on_state_callback(self.device_id, entity, state)
            except Exception:
                logger.exception(f"Error handling state of {entity.name} on {self.device_id}")

    async def _report_availability(self, available: bool, reason: str | None):
        if self.on_availability_callback is None or self._available == available:
            return
        self._available = available
        try:
            await self.on_availability_callback(self.device_id, available, reason)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception(f"Error reporting availability of {self.device_id}")

    async def report_client(self):
        """Tell the client callback the current client again, as if it had just connected."""
        self._reported_client = None
        await self._report_client(self._client)

    async def _report_client(self, client: APIClient | None):
        if self.on_client_callback is None or self._reported_client is client:
            return
        self._reported_client = client
        try:
            await self.on_client_callback(self.device_id, client)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception(f"Error reporting the client of {self.device_id}")

    async def _close_client(self):
        await self._report_client(None)
        client, self._client = self._client, None
        if client is not None:
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                await client.disconnect()

# FILE: majordom_esphome/controller.py

"""ESPHome integration controller for MajorDom."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import logging
import secrets
from collections.abc import Callable, Coroutine
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID

from aioesphomeapi import ZERO_NOISE_PSK, APIClient, EntityInfo, EntityState
from majordom_integration_sdk import (
    AbstractController,
    MissingCredentialsError,
    Need,
    PeripheralChange,
    Platform,
    WifiCredentials,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.capabilities import (
    BLE_ROUTER,
    ZEROCONF,
    BLEDiscoveryInfo,
    BLERouter,
    Zeroconf,
    ZeroconfDiscoveryInfo,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.files import read_json, write_json
from majordom_integration_sdk.peripherals import BLEProxy
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas import (
    CredentialsType,
    DeviceParameterChange,
    ProvidedCredentials,
)
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.command import DeviceCommand
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.device import Discovery
from majordom_integration_sdk.schemas.parameter import ParameterVisibility
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from . import improv, mapper
from .bluetooth import ble_source_of
from .connection import ESPhomeDeviceConnection, describe_error
from .models import (
    ESPhomeDevice,
    ESPhomeDeviceIntegrationData,
    ESPhomeParameter,
    ESPhomeParameterIntegrationData,
    ParameterSpec,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

NODE_APPEAR_TIMEOUT = 60.0  # seconds for a node to announce itself over mDNS once it has joined Wi-Fi


@dataclass
class _DiscoveryData:
    addresses: list[str]
    port: int
    mac: str | None
    keyless: bool  # encryption is on but no key is set: the integration gives the node one at pairing
    zero_psk: bool  # the keyless node takes its key over the zero PSK (older firmware: only in plaintext)


@dataclass
class _ImprovNode:
    """An unprovisioned node, waiting for Wi-Fi over BLE."""

    name: str  # its node name, as far as BLE carries it
    address: str


class ESPhomeController(AbstractController[ESPhomeDevice, ESPhomeParameter, "ESPhomeController.Settings"]):
    name = "ESPHome"  # its key, the slug "esphome", scopes its devices
    # Nodes are found over mDNS. Devices on Thread reach the hub through a border router; Wi-Fi devices need nothing.
    # The router sets unprovisioned nodes up over Improv BLE; the nodes that proxy Bluetooth are offered back to it.
    needs = [
        ZEROCONF,
        Need("thread", ["otbr-rest"], is_required=False),
        replace(BLE_ROUTER, is_required=False),
    ]

    class Settings(BaseModel):
        is_bluetooth_proxy_enabled: bool = Field(
            True,
            title="Bluetooth proxies",
            description="Reach Bluetooth devices through ESPHome devices with bluetooth_proxy. A device serves one hub "
            "at a time: turn this off only if another hub needs its Bluetooth proxy.",
        )

    def __init__(self, platform: Platform, *, settings: ESPhomeController.Settings | None = None):
        super().__init__(platform, settings=settings)
        self._connections: dict[UUID, ESPhomeDeviceConnection] = {}
        self._proxies: dict[UUID, BLEProxy] = {}  # the nodes lending their Bluetooth radio to the hub
        self._discoveries: dict[UUID, Discovery] = {}
        self._discovery_data: dict[UUID, _DiscoveryData] = {}
        self._discovery_names: dict[str, UUID] = {}  # mDNS record name -> discovery id, for goodbyes
        self._zeroconf_cancel: Callable[[], None] | None = None
        self._ble_cancel: Callable[[], None] | None = None
        self._improv_nodes: dict[UUID, _ImprovNode] = {}
        self._ble_names: dict[str, str] = {}  # BLE address -> advertised name: ESPHome sends it in few adverts
        self._joining: dict[str, asyncio.Future[Discovery]] = {}  # BLE name -> the node's mDNS discovery, once seen
        self._paired: set[UUID] = set()
        self._tasks: set[asyncio.Task[Any]] = set()
        self._states: dict[UUID, dict[int, EntityState]] = {}
        self._run: object | None = None  # from start() to stop(): a pairing finishing in another run adopts nothing

    @property
    def discoveries(self) -> dict[UUID, Discovery]:
        return self._discoveries.copy()

    @property
    def provides(self) -> list[BLEProxy]:
        return list(self._proxies.values())

    @property
    def device_type(self) -> type[ESPhomeDevice]:
        return ESPhomeDevice

    @property
    def parameter_type(self) -> type[ESPhomeParameter]:
        return ESPhomeParameter

    # Lifecycle

    async def start(self):
        logger.info("Starting ESPHome integration")
        self._run = object()
        await self._load_paired_devices()  # first: DNS-SD tells the nodes in its cache at once, the paired ones too

        if (zeroconf := self.peripherals.instance(ZEROCONF)) is None:
            raise RuntimeError("zeroconf isn't bound")
        self._zeroconf_cancel = zeroconf.register(self, services={"_esphomelib._tcp.local."})
        self._listen_for_improv()

    async def stop(self):
        logger.info("Stopping ESPHome integration")
        self._run = None
        if self._zeroconf_cancel:
            self._zeroconf_cancel()
            self._zeroconf_cancel = None
        if self._ble_cancel:
            self._ble_cancel()
            self._ble_cancel = None

        tasks = list(self._tasks)  # the setups over Bluetooth too
        for task in tasks:
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
        for connection in list(self._connections.values()):
            await connection.stop()
        self._connections.clear()
        for device_id in list(self._proxies):
            await self._on_client(device_id, None)
        self._states.clear()
        self._paired.clear()
        # heard anew after a start, which reports them again; a node that left meanwhile says no goodbye
        self._discoveries.clear()
        self._discovery_data.clear()
        self._discovery_names.clear()
        self._improv_nodes.clear()
        self._ble_names.clear()

    async def needed_peripheral_did_change(self, change: PeripheralChange) -> bool:
        """The router is followed in place, and a border router only carries the Thread devices to the hub: neither
        restarts it. Another DNS-SD does."""
        if change.family == "ble":
            await self._let_go_of_router()
            self._listen_for_improv()
        return change.family in ("ble", "thread")

    # Hub -> device

    async def pair_device(self, discovery: Discovery, credentials: ProvidedCredentials | None) -> UUID | None:
        run = self._run
        if discovery.id in self._improv_nodes:
            return await self._pair_over_ble(discovery, run)
        await self._pair_over_api(discovery, credentials, run)
        return None

    async def unpair(self, device: ESPhomeDevice):
        connection = self._connections.pop(device.id, None)
        self._states.pop(device.id, None)
        self._paired.discard(device.id)
        if connection:
            await connection.stop()
        # The Hub removes the device record after unpair; the repository protocol
        # intentionally does not expose delete() to integrations.

    async def identify(self, device: ESPhomeDevice):
        # ESPHome has no identify action, so there is nothing to send to the device
        logger.info(f"Identify called for {device.id}: not supported by ESPHome")

    async def fetch(self, device: ESPhomeDevice):
        if device.id not in self._connections:
            raise ConnectionError("Device not connected")
        await self._report_snapshot(device.id)

    async def send_command(
        self,
        command: DeviceCommand,
        device: ESPhomeDevice,
        parameter: ESPhomeParameter,
    ):
        data = parameter.integration_data
        if mapper.is_local(parameter):  # a setting kept here: stored, and echoed so the Hub stores it too
            await self._keep_setting(device.id, data.object_id or "", data.sub_field or "", parameter, command.value)
            return

        connection = self._connections.get(device.id)
        if connection is None or not connection.ready:
            await self._update_device(device.id, last_error=f"{parameter.name} could not be set: device not connected")
            raise ConnectionError("Device not connected")

        stored = await self._update_device(device.id)
        settings = stored.integration_data.settings.get(data.object_id or "", {}) if stored is not None else {}
        args = mapper.build_command_args(parameter, command.value, self._states.get(device.id, {}), settings)
        try:
            await connection.send_command(args["key"], data.component_type, args)
        except ConnectionError:
            await self._update_device(device.id, last_error=f"{parameter.name} could not be set: device not connected")
            raise
        await self._update_device(device.id, last_error=None)

    # ZeroconfDiscoveryListener: called by the SDK's discovery service

    async def zeroconf_did_discover_service(self, zeroconf: Zeroconf, info: ZeroconfDiscoveryInfo):
        await self._on_zeroconf_service(info)

    async def zeroconf_did_update_service(self, zeroconf: Zeroconf, info: ZeroconfDiscoveryInfo):
        await self._on_zeroconf_service(info)

    async def zeroconf_did_remove_service(self, zeroconf: Zeroconf, type_: str, name: str):
        device_id = self._discovery_names.pop(name, None)
        if device_id is not None and self._discoveries.pop(device_id, None) is not None:
            self._discovery_data.pop(device_id, None)
            await self.output.controller_did_lose_discovery(self, device_id)

    # BLEDiscoveryListener: unprovisioned nodes advertising Improv

    async def ble_did_discover_device(self, ble: BLERouter, info: BLEDiscoveryInfo):
        await self._on_improv_advert(info)

    async def ble_did_update_device(self, ble: BLERouter, info: BLEDiscoveryInfo):
        await self._on_improv_advert(info)

    async def ble_did_remove_device(self, ble: BLERouter, info: BLEDiscoveryInfo):
        if self._ble_names.get(info.device.address) in self._joining:  # set up: it stops advertising once on Wi-Fi
            return
        await self._lose_improv_node(info.device.address)

    # Private: discovery

    async def _on_zeroconf_service(self, service_info: ZeroconfDiscoveryInfo):
        try:
            node_name = service_info.name.removesuffix(f".{service_info.type_}")
            properties = service_info.decoded_properties
            mac = properties.get("mac")
            device_id = self.device_uuid(mac or node_name)
            addresses = self._announced_addresses(service_info, node_name)
            if device_id in self._paired:
                await self._refresh_addresses(device_id, addresses)
                await self._refuse_setup(node_name, device_id)
                return
            port = service_info.port or 6053
            # a key is configured: the user's, unless it is one this integration gave the node in an earlier attempt.
            # Even then the user may enter one: the node may have been reflashed with a key of its own since.
            if "api_encryption" not in properties:
                credentials_options = [CredentialsType.none]
            elif await self._kept_key(device_id, mac) is None:
                credentials_options = [CredentialsType.secret]
            else:
                credentials_options = [CredentialsType.none, CredentialsType.secret]

            discovery = Discovery(
                id=device_id,
                integration=self.key,
                transport="tcp",
                device_manufacturer="esphome",
                device_name=properties.get("friendly_name") or node_name,
                device_category=None,  # a node may host anything
                device_icon=None,
                expected_credentials_options=credentials_options,
            )
            keyless = "api_encryption_supported" in properties
            zero_psk = properties.get("api_provisioning") == "zero-psk"
            self._discovery_data[device_id] = _DiscoveryData(addresses, port, mac, keyless, zero_psk)
            self._discovery_names[service_info.name] = device_id
            for ble_name, joined in self._joining.items():
                if improv.is_node(ble_name, node_name) and not joined.done():
                    joined.set_result(discovery)
            known = self._discoveries.get(device_id)
            if known == discovery:
                return
            self._discoveries[device_id] = discovery
            if known is None:
                await self.output.controller_did_receive_discovery(self, discovery)
            else:
                await self.output.controller_did_update_discovery(self, discovery)
            logger.debug(f"Discovered ESPHome node {node_name} at {addresses}:{port}")
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Error handling zeroconf discovery")

    @property
    def _router(self) -> BLERouter | None:
        return self.peripherals.instance(BLE_ROUTER)

    async def _let_go_of_router(self):
        """Stop listening to the router, and lose the nodes it heard: the next one tells what it hears."""
        if self._ble_cancel:
            self._ble_cancel()
            self._ble_cancel = None
        lost = [device_id for device_id in self._improv_nodes if self._discoveries.pop(device_id, None) is not None]
        self._improv_nodes.clear()
        self._ble_names.clear()
        for device_id in lost:
            await self.output.controller_did_lose_discovery(self, device_id)

    def _listen_for_improv(self):
        """Hear unprovisioned nodes through the router bound now, if there is one."""
        router = self._router
        self._ble_cancel = router.register(self, {UUID(improv.SERVICE_UUID)}) if router else None

    async def _lose_improv_node(self, address: str):
        name = self._ble_names.pop(address, None)
        device_id = self.device_uuid(f"improv:{name}") if name else None
        if device_id is not None and self._discoveries.pop(device_id, None) is not None:
            self._improv_nodes.pop(device_id, None)
            await self.output.controller_did_lose_discovery(self, device_id)

    async def _on_improv_advert(self, info: BLEDiscoveryInfo):
        """Offer a node waiting for Wi-Fi. Improv carries no identity but the node name, so the discovery is keyed by
        it (the BLE address may be random, and differs from the MAC the node is known by once on the network)."""
        try:
            name = info.advertisement.local_name or self._ble_names.get(info.device.address)
            if name is None or not improv.waits_for_wifi(info.advertisement):
                return
            self._ble_names[info.device.address] = name
            device_id = self.device_uuid(f"improv:{name}")
            self._improv_nodes[device_id] = _ImprovNode(name, info.device.address)
            if device_id in self._discoveries:  # adverts repeat all the time: keep the discovery (and its last error)
                return
            discovery = Discovery(
                id=device_id,
                integration=self.key,
                transport="ble",
                device_manufacturer="esphome",
                device_name=name,
                device_category=None,
                device_icon=None,
                expected_credentials_options=[CredentialsType.none],  # the Hub gives it its own Wi-Fi
            )
            self._discoveries[device_id] = discovery
            await self.output.controller_did_receive_discovery(self, discovery)
            logger.debug(f"Discovered unprovisioned ESPHome node {name} over BLE")
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Error handling BLE discovery")

    @staticmethod
    def _announced_addresses(info: ZeroconfDiscoveryInfo, node_name: str) -> list[str]:
        """Hostname first (it follows the device through DHCP changes), then the announced IPs."""
        hostname = info.server.rstrip(".") if info.server else None
        addresses = [hostname, *(info.parsed_addresses or [])] if hostname else list(info.parsed_addresses or [])
        return list(dict.fromkeys(addresses)) or [f"{node_name}.local"]

    async def _refresh_addresses(self, device_id: UUID, announced: list[str]):
        """A paired device announced itself again: learn its new addresses, forget the ones it left."""
        device = await self._update_device(device_id)
        if device is None:
            return
        known = device.integration_data.addresses
        refreshed = [a for a in announced if a not in known] + [a for a in known if a in announced]
        if refreshed == known:
            return
        logger.info(f"Addresses of {device_id} changed: {known} -> {refreshed}")
        await self._save_integration_data(device_id, addresses=refreshed)
        if connection := self._connections.get(device_id):
            connection.addresses = refreshed

    async def _refuse_setup(self, node_name: str, device_id: UUID):
        """A node set up over BLE announced itself as a paired one (its Wi-Fi was reset): it is back, and its device
        reconnects. Its setup fails rather than replace that device."""
        joining = [joined for ble_name, joined in self._joining.items() if improv.is_node(ble_name, node_name)]
        if not joining:
            return
        device = await self._update_device(device_id)
        name = device.name if device is not None else node_name
        for joined in joining:
            if not joined.done():
                joined.set_exception(ValueError(f"The device is already paired as {name}: it is back on the network"))

    # Private: connections and state

    async def _load_paired_devices(self):
        async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repo:
            devices = await repo.get_all(ESPhomeDevice)
        for device in devices:
            if device.integration_data.addresses:  # else the Hub created it, but its pairing never completed
                self._paired.add(device.id)
                self._connect(device)

    def _connect(self, device: ESPhomeDevice):
        data = device.integration_data
        connection = self._make_connection(device.id, data.addresses, data.port, data.encryption_key)
        self._connections[device.id] = connection
        self._spawn(connection.start())

    def _make_connection(
        self, device_id: UUID, addresses: list[str], port: int, encryption_key: str | None
    ) -> ESPhomeDeviceConnection:
        return ESPhomeDeviceConnection(
            device_id=device_id,
            addresses=addresses,
            port=port,
            encryption_key=encryption_key,
            on_state=self._on_state,
            on_availability=self._on_availability,
            on_addresses=self._on_addresses,
            on_client=self._on_client if self.settings.is_bluetooth_proxy_enabled else None,
        )

    def _spawn[T](self, coroutine: Coroutine[Any, Any, T]) -> asyncio.Task[T]:
        """Run in the background, keeping a reference so the task is neither collected nor left behind on stop()."""
        task = asyncio.create_task(coroutine)
        self._tasks.add(task)
        task.add_done_callback(self._tasks.discard)
        return task

    async def _on_availability(self, device_id: UUID, available: bool, reason: str | None):
        if device_id not in self._connections:  # still pairing, or already unpaired
            return
        await self._update_device(device_id, available=available, last_error=None if available else reason)
        if available:
            await self.output.controller_did_connect_device(self, device_id)
        else:
            await self.output.controller_did_lose_device(self, device_id)

    async def _on_client(self, device_id: UUID, client: APIClient | None):
        """A paired node connected: lend its Bluetooth radio, if it has one to lend, as a ``ble/esphome-proxy`` the
        router takes; a node being paired serves no one until it is. A node gone: take the radio back."""
        if client is None:
            if self._proxies.pop(device_id, None):
                await self.output.controller_did_change_provided(self)
        elif device_id in self._connections and (source := await ble_source_of(client)):
            self._proxies[device_id] = BLEProxy(source, name=source.mac)
            await self.output.controller_did_change_provided(self)

    async def _on_addresses(self, device_id: UUID, addresses: list[str]):
        if device_id in self._connections:  # not while pairing: the device is saved with the final order
            await self._save_integration_data(device_id, addresses=addresses)

    async def _update_device(self, device_id: UUID, **changes: Any) -> ESPhomeDevice | None:
        async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repo:
            device = await repo.get(device_id, as_=ESPhomeDevice)
            if device is None:
                return None
            if any(getattr(device, field) != value for field, value in changes.items()):
                device = device.model_copy(update=changes)
                await repo.save(device)
            return device

    async def _save_integration_data(self, device_id: UUID, **changes: Any):
        async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repo:
            device = await repo.get(device_id, as_=ESPhomeDevice)
            if device is not None:
                data = device.integration_data.model_copy(update=changes)
                await repo.save(device.model_copy(update={"integration_data": data}))

    async def _on_state(self, device_id: UUID, entity: EntityInfo, state: EntityState):
        self._states.setdefault(device_id, {})[state.key] = state  # kept while pairing: the snapshot then reports them
        if device_id not in self._connections:  # still pairing, or already unpaired: the Hub does not know the device
            return
        try:
            events = self._events(device_id, entity, state)
            if events:
                await self.output.controller_did_receive_events(self, events)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception(f"Error handling state for {entity.name}")

    def _events(self, device_id: UUID, entity: EntityInfo, state: EntityState) -> list[DeviceParameterChange]:
        component = mapper.component_type_of(entity)
        if component is None:
            return []
        exposed = {spec.sub_field: spec for spec in mapper.parameter_specs(entity, component)}
        events = []
        for sub_field, value in mapper.state_values(entity, state).items():
            spec = exposed.get(sub_field)
            if spec is None:
                continue
            if spec.fields:  # a struct value: keyed by the sub-parameter ids, as the SDK specifies
                value = {
                    str(self._parameter_id(device_id, entity, f"{sub_field}.{name}")): v for name, v in value.items()
                }
            parameter_id = self._parameter_id(device_id, entity, sub_field)
            events.append(DeviceParameterChange(device_id=device_id, parameter_id=parameter_id, value=value))
        return events

    @staticmethod
    def _visibility(entity: EntityInfo, spec: ParameterSpec) -> ParameterVisibility:
        """The entity's own visibility, unless the spec asks for a less prominent one (and the entity allows it)."""
        visibility = mapper.visibility_of(entity)
        if spec.visibility == ParameterVisibility.system:  # infrastructure is hidden whatever the entity says
            return spec.visibility
        return spec.visibility if visibility == ParameterVisibility.user and spec.visibility else visibility

    def _parameter_id(self, device_id: UUID, entity: EntityInfo, sub_field: str) -> UUID:
        return self.parameter_uuid(device_id, f"{entity.object_id}_{sub_field}")

    async def _report_snapshot(self, device_id: UUID):
        """Report the last known value of every parameter in a single batch, the kept settings included."""
        connection = self._connections[device_id]
        entities = connection.get_entities()
        events = [
            event
            for key, state in self._states.get(device_id, {}).items()
            if key in entities
            for event in self._events(device_id, entities[key], state)
        ]
        device = await self._update_device(device_id)
        settings = device.integration_data.settings if device is not None else {}
        for entity in entities.values():
            for field, value in settings.get(entity.object_id, {}).items():
                if value is None:  # a cleared setting
                    continue
                parameter_id = self._parameter_id(device_id, entity, field)
                events.append(DeviceParameterChange(device_id=device_id, parameter_id=parameter_id, value=value))
        if events:
            await self.output.controller_did_receive_events(self, events)

    def _build_parameter(
        self, device_id: UUID, entity: EntityInfo, component: str, spec: ParameterSpec, parent: str | None = None
    ) -> ESPhomeParameter:
        path = (
            f"{parent}.{spec.sub_field}" if parent else spec.sub_field
        )  # a sub-parameter's id is scoped to its parent
        label = spec.sub_field.replace("_", " ")
        name = label.capitalize() if parent else entity.name if spec.sub_field == "state" else f"{entity.name} {label}"
        return ESPhomeParameter(
            id=self._parameter_id(device_id, entity, path),
            name=name,
            data_type=spec.data_type,
            role=spec.role,
            unit=spec.unit,
            min_value=spec.min_value,
            max_value=spec.max_value,
            min_step=spec.min_step,
            valid_values=spec.valid_values,
            visibility=self._visibility(entity, spec),
            fields=[self._build_parameter(device_id, entity, component, child, path) for child in spec.fields] or None,
            integration_data=ESPhomeParameterIntegrationData(
                entity_name=entity.name,
                object_id=entity.object_id,
                component_type=component,
                parameter_type=mapper.PARAMETER_TYPE.get(component, mapper.ESPhomeParameterType.STATE),
                service_key=entity.key,
                sub_field=spec.sub_field,
            ),
        )

    async def _keep_setting(self, device_id: UUID, object_id: str, field: str, parameter: ESPhomeParameter, value: Any):
        kept = mapper.local_value(parameter, value)
        async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repo:
            device = await repo.get(device_id, as_=ESPhomeDevice)
            if device is None:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown device {device_id}")
            settings = {**device.integration_data.settings}
            settings[object_id] = {**settings.get(object_id, {}), field: kept}
            data = device.integration_data.model_copy(update={"settings": settings})
            await repo.save(device.model_copy(update={"integration_data": data}))
        event = DeviceParameterChange(device_id=device_id, parameter_id=parameter.id, value=kept)
        await self.output.controller_did_receive_events(self, [event])

    # Private: pairing

    async def _pair_over_ble(self, discovery: Discovery, run: object | None) -> UUID:
        """Give the node the Hub's Wi-Fi, wait for it on the network, then pair it like any other node. The Hub's device
        takes the node's own identity (from its MAC), which is what it is found by from then on; it is returned."""
        logger.info(f"Setting up ESPHome device {discovery.device_name} over BLE")
        node = self._improv_nodes[discovery.id]
        try:
            wifi = self._wifi_credentials()
            async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repo:
                hub_device = await repo.get(discovery.id, as_=ESPhomeDevice)
            if hub_device is None:
                raise LookupError("The Hub has not created a device for this discovery")
            if (router := self._router) is None:
                raise LookupError("The Hub has no Bluetooth to set the device up with")
            setup = self._spawn(self._join_wifi(router, node, wifi, discovery.id))  # stop() ends it at once
            try:
                on_network = await setup
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                self._refuse_if_stopped(run)  # stop() ended it
                raise  # the Hub's request went away
            self._refuse_if_stopped(run)
            async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repo:
                await repo.save(hub_device.model_copy(update={"id": on_network.id}), previous_id=discovery.id)
            await self._pair_over_api(on_network, None, run)
        except MissingCredentialsError:
            raise  # the Hub returns it to the app's pairing request
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.exception(f"Setting up {discovery.device_name} over BLE failed")
            reason = str(exc) if isinstance(exc, ValueError | LookupError | TimeoutError | improv.SetupError) else None
            await self._report_error(discovery.id, reason or describe_error(exc.__cause__ or exc))
            router = self._router
            if router is None or node.address not in {info.device.address for info in router.devices()}:
                await self._lose_improv_node(node.address)  # its removal came while it was set up: none comes again
            raise
        self._discoveries.pop(discovery.id, None)
        self._improv_nodes.pop(discovery.id, None)
        # the Hub paired the node through its BLE discovery: the one it announced over mDNS is gone too
        await self.output.controller_did_lose_discovery(self, on_network.id)
        return on_network.id

    async def _join_wifi(
        self, router: BLERouter, node: _ImprovNode, wifi: WifiCredentials, discovery_id: UUID
    ) -> Discovery:
        """Give the node the Hub's Wi-Fi over Improv, then wait for it on the network: its mDNS discovery."""
        joined = self._joining[node.name] = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
        try:
            await improv.provision(
                router,
                node.address,
                wifi.ssid,
                wifi.password,
                on_authorization_required=lambda: self._report_error(discovery_id, improv.PRESS_BUTTON),
            )
            async with asyncio.timeout(NODE_APPEAR_TIMEOUT):
                return await joined
        except TimeoutError:
            raise TimeoutError(f"The device joined {wifi.ssid} but did not show up on the network") from None
        finally:
            self._joining.pop(node.name, None)

    def _wifi_credentials(self) -> WifiCredentials:
        if (wifi := self.platform.wifi) is None:
            raise MissingCredentialsError(MissingCredentialsError.WIFI)
        return wifi

    async def _report_error(self, discovery_id: UUID, reason: str):
        """Show the user why pairing a discovery failed (or what it waits for), while it is still offered."""
        if (known := self._discoveries.get(discovery_id)) is not None:
            failed = known.model_copy(update={"last_error": reason})
            self._discoveries[discovery_id] = failed
            await self.output.controller_did_update_discovery(self, failed)

    async def _pair_over_api(self, discovery: Discovery, credentials: ProvidedCredentials | None, run: object | None):
        logger.info(f"Pairing ESPHome device: {discovery.id}")
        known = self._discoveries.get(discovery.id, discovery)
        conn: ESPhomeDeviceConnection | None = None
        try:
            integration_data = self._discovery_data.get(discovery.id)
            if integration_data is None:
                raise ValueError("Unknown device: it is no longer discovered")
            credentials_type = credentials.type if credentials else CredentialsType.none
            if credentials_type not in known.expected_credentials_options:
                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported credentials for this device: {credentials_type}")
            encryption_key = credentials.value if credentials and credentials_type == CredentialsType.secret else None
            if credentials_type == CredentialsType.secret and not encryption_key:
                raise ValueError("The encryption key is required for this device")
            async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repo:
                hub_device = await repo.get(
                    discovery.id, as_=ESPhomeDevice
                )  # the Hub creates the device before pairing
            if hub_device is None:
                raise LookupError("The Hub has not created a device for this discovery")

            encryption_key = (
                encryption_key or hub_device.integration_data.encryption_key or self._given_key(integration_data.mac)
            )

            conn = self._make_connection(
                discovery.id, integration_data.addresses, integration_data.port, encryption_key
            )
            if integration_data.keyless:
                encryption_key = await self._provision_key(conn, integration_data, encryption_key)
            elif encryption_key is None:
                logger.warning(
                    f"{discovery.device_name} accepts unencrypted API connections only: "
                    "add `api: encryption:` to its YAML"
                )
            await conn.start()
            await conn.wait_ready()

            parameters = [
                self._build_parameter(discovery.id, entity, component, spec)
                for entity in conn.get_entities().values()
                if (component := mapper.component_type_of(entity)) is not None
                for spec in mapper.parameter_specs(entity, component)
            ]
            main = next((p.id for p in parameters if p.can_be_main_parameter and p.role == "control"), None)

            device = hub_device.model_copy(
                update={
                    "parameters": parameters,
                    "main_parameter": main,
                    "available": True,
                    "last_error": None,
                    "integration_data": ESPhomeDeviceIntegrationData(
                        device_name=discovery.device_name,
                        unique_id=integration_data.mac,
                        mac_address=integration_data.mac,
                        addresses=conn.addresses,
                        port=integration_data.port,
                        encryption_key=encryption_key,
                    ),
                }
            )

            self._refuse_if_stopped(run)
            async with self.platform.device_repository(self) as repo:
                await repo.save(device)

            self._refuse_if_stopped(run)  # it stopped while the device was saved
            self._connections[discovery.id] = conn
            self._paired.add(discovery.id)
            if credentials_type == CredentialsType.secret:
                self._forget_given_key(integration_data.mac)

            await self.output.controller_did_connect_device(self, discovery.id)
            await self._report_snapshot(discovery.id)
            await conn.report_client()  # paired: its radio may serve the hub now
            self._discoveries.pop(discovery.id, None)
            self._discovery_data.pop(discovery.id, None)

        except asyncio.CancelledError:  # no one waits for the outcome: let go of the node
            await self._let_go_of_pairing(discovery.id, conn)
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            await self._let_go_of_pairing(discovery.id, conn)
            logger.exception(f"Pairing {discovery.id} failed")
            if self._is_current(run):  # a stopped controller offers nothing
                reason = str(exc) if isinstance(exc, ValueError | LookupError) else describe_error(exc.__cause__ or exc)
                failed = known.model_copy(update={"last_error": reason})
                self._discoveries[discovery.id] = failed
                await self.output.controller_did_update_discovery(self, failed)
            raise

    async def _let_go_of_pairing(self, device_id: UUID, conn: ESPhomeDeviceConnection | None):
        """Undo a pairing that didn't finish: its node connection goes, also once taken in, so it can be tried again."""
        if conn is not None:
            await conn.stop()
            if self._connections.get(device_id) is conn:
                del self._connections[device_id]
                self._paired.discard(device_id)
        self._states.pop(device_id, None)

    def _refuse_if_stopped(self, run: object | None):
        """A pairing that finishes after stop() takes nothing, also once ESPHome runs again (that run may have other
        settings): the next start() connects what is paired anew. Adopting it into the new run may come later."""
        if not self._is_current(run):
            raise ConnectionError("ESPHome stopped while pairing")

    def _is_current(self, run: object | None) -> bool:
        return run is not None and run is self._run

    # Private: encryption keys

    async def _kept_key(self, device_id: UUID, mac: str | None) -> str | None:
        device = await self._update_device(device_id)
        return (device.integration_data.encryption_key if device is not None else None) or self._given_key(mac)

    @property
    def _keys_file(self) -> Path:
        return self.platform.documents_folder(self) / "keys.json"

    def _given_key(self, mac: str | None) -> str | None:
        """The key given to the node with ``mac``, kept apart from the Hub's device record too: the Hub deletes the
        record when a pairing fails, and after unpairing it, though the node requires the key from then on. Forgotten
        only once the node is paired with a key the user typed (it was reflashed with one of its own)."""
        return read_json(self._keys_file).get(mac) if mac else None

    def _forget_given_key(self, mac: str | None):
        keys = read_json(self._keys_file)
        if keys.pop(mac or "", None):
            write_json(self._keys_file, keys)

    async def _provision_key(self, conn: ESPhomeDeviceConnection, data: _DiscoveryData, key: str | None) -> str:
        """Give a keyless node a key of our own (or the one kept from an earlier attempt). It is kept before it is
        set: from then on the node accepts nothing else, so losing it would lock the Hub out until a factory reset."""
        key = key or base64.b64encode(secrets.token_bytes(32)).decode()
        await self._save_integration_data(conn.device_id, encryption_key=key)
        if data.mac:
            write_json(self._keys_file, {**read_json(self._keys_file), data.mac: key})
        await conn.provision_key(key, ZERO_NOISE_PSK if data.zero_psk else None)
        data.keyless = False  # whatever mDNS still announces, the node requires the key now
        return key
